reconstructed_theorem_text: Let E be any finite-dimensional real inner-product space with its induced norm and Borel sigma-algebra. Let gamma_E be the centered Gaussian probability measure on E with covariance the identity. Let L^2(gamma_E; R) be the real Hilbert space of square-integrable real-valued functions modulo gamma_E-almost-everywhere equality. Write H_j for the unnormalized probabilists' Hermite polynomial of degree j, with its integer coefficients interpreted in R (H_0(t)=1, H_1(t)=t, and H_(n+1)(t)=t H_n(t)-n H_(n-1)(t) for n>=1). Define Phi_j(w)=[x |-> H_j(<w,x>)] in L^2(gamma_E; R), where brackets denote the almost-everywhere equivalence class of the literal square-integrable function displayed. For each finite set s of nonnegative integers, each arbitrary coefficient sequence c:N -> R, and each w in E, the declaration defines F_(s,c)(w)=sum_(j in s) c(j) Phi_j(w), where the sum and scalar multiplication are taken in L^2(gamma_E; R). Equivalently its value is the class [x |-> sum_(j in s) c(j) H_j(<w,x>)]. Its type is Finset(N) -> (N -> R) -> E -> L^2(gamma_E; R); its body is precisely the displayed finite linear combination. The empty-set sum is the zero L^2 class.
objects: Hermite classes Phi_j(w) and the defined finite feature F_(s,c)(w).
domains: s a finite subset of N including possibly zero or no elements; c any N -> R; w and x in E; values in L^2(gamma_E; R).
quantifiers: For every E, s, c, and w of these types, the definition supplies F_(s,c)(w).
assumptions: Finite-dimensional real inner-product space with Borel measurable structure; s is finite. No support, sign, summability, or nonvanishing condition is imposed on c.
conclusion: Definition F_(s,c)(w)=sum_(j in s) c(j)[x |-> H_j(<w,x>)].
scopes: Finite sum in the actual L^2 space, defined for every ambient w in E.
constant_dependencies: The value depends on E with its inner product, s, the values c(j) for j in s, and w. Coefficients outside s play no role. No bound constant occurs.
semantic_notes: This is a definition rather than a theorem about regularity or inner products.
An arbitrary coefficient sequence is permitted because only the finite set s is summed.
Equality to the displayed sum of literal functions is understood at the L^2 class level, not as a pointwise identity for a chosen representative.
